svg.title: HGS key rollover without stranding existing VM state
svg.desc: Read five stages downward. HGS administrators stage new keys and prove private-key access on every node. They select the new primary keys and publish authenticated metadata. VM owners update existing key protectors without replacing their protected secret. Teams test current VMs and retained recovery states, including negative authorization tests. Only then are old keys disabled and retired according to approved retention and compromise decisions. New primary selection does not rewrite old VMs or backups.
svg.text: Key rollover: preserve authorization through change
Primary-key selection alone does not rewrite existing VMs or backups.

g.text: 1. HGS administrators stage new keys
Check the required KSP certificate profile and approved key identities.
Prove usable signing and encryption private keys on every HGS node.
Provision HSM or thumbprint-based key access per node as required.
2. Select primary keys and publish metadata
Make the approved keys primary for the intended operations.
Owners authenticate the new fabric guardian identities out of band.
Existing protected state can still depend on the old keys.
3. Owners update existing key protectors
Keep each VM off during the approved KP exchange.
Grant or revoke guardian access without replacing the protected secret.
Creating a new PDK does not update deployed VM key protectors.
4. Test current and retained recovery states
Cover VMs, PDKs, checkpoints, replicas, and retained backups.
Prove authorized starts and rejection by unauthorized destinations.
Inspect old KPs before reconnecting a restored VM.
5. Disable, then retire old keys deliberately
Meet the approved transition and recovery-retention conditions first.
Routine rotation may allow a controlled overlap; compromise differs.
Never silently restore compromised trust to make a backup start.

svg.text: Same-key renewal and new-key rollover have different recovery consequences.
A matching certificate subject name is not the same cryptographic key.
